components.note: 女 (woman) — women and relatives: 妈, 姐, 姑; 奶 is milk or a grandmother.
乃 (nǎi) sounds exactly like 奶.
女 (woman) — women and relatives: 妈, 姐, 姑; 奶 is milk or a grandmother.
乃 (nǎi) sounds exactly like 奶.

example.hanzi: 我奶奶今年八十岁了,身体还很健康。
example.pinyin: Wǒ nǎinai jīnnián bāshí suì le, shēntǐ hái hěn jiànkāng.
example.english: My grandma is eighty this year and still in good health.
example.fact: Chinese kinship terms are far more specific than English's single "grandma" — 奶奶 names your father's mother specifically, while your mother's mother is a different word, 外婆 (or 姥姥 in northern usage) — the two sides of the family tree are never collapsed into one shared term the way English does.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǎinai zhù zài xiāngxià.
examples.english: My grandmother lives in the countryside.

examples.pinyin: Nǎinai gěi wǒ zuòle hóngshāoròu.
examples.english: Grandma made me braised pork.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — marks wine and brewing, as in 酒, 醉 drunk, 醒; 配 first meant mixing wine, then matching.
己 (jǐ) is only a loose sound hint for pèi.

example.hanzi: 这条裙子配这双鞋很好看。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi pèi zhè shuāng xié hěn hǎokàn.
example.english: This skirt looks nice with these shoes.
example.fact: 配 means to match, complement or dispense: 配合 (cooperate), 配套 (matching set), 配菜 (side dish), 配眼镜 (get glasses made). It also means to be worthy of: 他不配 ("he doesn't deserve it").

examples.hanzi: 这个红色的包配你的外套很好看。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hóngsè de bāo pèi nǐ de wàitào hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: This red bag goes well with your coat.

examples.pinyin: Tā pèibushàng tā.
examples.english: He doesn't deserve her.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.
氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: water draining away.
肖 (xiāo) gives the exact sound; also in 销 xiāo and 削 xuē.

example.hanzi: 因为天气不好,航班被取消了。
example.pinyin: Yīnwèi tiānqì bù hǎo, hángbān bèi qǔxiāo le.
example.english: The flight was canceled because of bad weather.
example.fact: 取消 reads almost literally as "take away until it vanishes" — 取 ("to take, obtain," from an old image of taking an ear as spoils) plus 消 ("to dissolve, vanish") — a small window into how many Chinese two-character verbs are built by stacking a concrete action onto its intended result.

examples.hanzi: 会议取消了，大家可以回家了。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì qǔxiāo le, dàjiā kěyǐ huí jiā le.
examples.english: The meeting is canceled, so everyone can go home.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qǔxiāo dìngdān.
examples.english: I'd like to cancel my order.

components.note: 離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 他们结婚三年后决定离婚。
example.pinyin: Tāmen jiéhūn sān nián hòu juédìng líhūn.
example.english: They decided to divorce three years after getting married.
example.fact: 离婚 and 结婚 ("to marry") form a natural opposite pair through their first characters alone — 离 ("to leave, separate") versus 结 ("to tie, bind") — a vivid shared image of marriage as a knot and divorce as its undoing.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen yǐjīng líhūn sān nián le.
examples.english: They have been divorced for three years.

examples.hanzi: 她不想离婚，想再试一试。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng líhūn, xiǎng zài shì yi shì.
examples.english: She doesn't want a divorce and wants to try again.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips arranged in an even row; 等 means "rank, equal" and then "wait".
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for děng; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得; 待 is to go toward and wait on someone.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue; its family varies: 诗 shī, 持 chí, 特 tè, 等 děng.

example.hanzi: 我们已经等待这个结果很久了。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yǐjīng děngdài zhège jiéguǒ hěn jiǔ le.
example.english: We have been waiting for this result for a long time.
example.fact: 等待 is the formal, written-register partner of the everyday verb 等 — you'd say 等我一下 ("wait for me a sec") in casual speech, but a news report or literary text would more likely reach for 等待, as in 等待救援 ("waiting for rescue").

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ děngdài.
examples.english: Please wait here.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài děngdài hǎo xiāoxi.
examples.english: We are waiting for good news.

components.note: 友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 这部小说讲的是一段悲伤的爱情故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō jiǎng de shì yí duàn bēishāng de àiqíng gùshi.
example.english: This novel tells a sad love story.
example.fact: Chinese splits "love" by object in a way English doesn't: 爱情 is reserved specifically for romantic love between partners, while love for family, friends, or country uses plain 爱 or compounds like 亲情 (family love) and 友情 (friendship) — there's no single all-purpose word covering every kind of love the way English "love" does.

examples.hanzi: 他们的爱情故事很感人。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de àiqíng gùshi hěn gǎnrén.
examples.english: Their love story is very touching.

examples.pinyin: Niánqīngrén chángcháng tán àiqíng.
examples.english: Young people often talk about love.

components.note: 尺 (chǐ, ruler) — the visible top part, as in 尺寸 size. 尽 simplifies 盡 and the shape does not explain 'use up'. Memory aid: measure it to the very end.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 不管结果如何,我都会尽力。
example.pinyin: Bùguǎn jiéguǒ rúhé, wǒ dōu huì jìnlì.
example.english: No matter what the result is, I'll do my best.
example.fact: 尽力 literally means "to exhaust one's strength" (尽 "to use up completely" + 力 "strength, power") — the same 尽 root shows up in 尽量 ("as much as possible") and 尽情 ("to one's heart's content"), all sharing the sense of pushing something all the way to its limit.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì jìnlì bāng nǐ.
examples.english: I'll do my best to help you.

examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì, wǒ jìnlì le.
examples.english: I gave it my all on this exam.

components.note: 十 (ten) — a cross: first a single vertical line, later crossed with a horizontal bar. Seen in 十分, 二十, and in 千.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.hanzi: 这个消息让大家十分惊讶。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi ràng dàjiā shífēn jīngyà.
example.english: This news made everyone extremely surprised.
example.fact: 十分 literally means "ten parts" — the same logic as saying something is "a hundred percent" true in English — turning a picture of a whole divided into ten complete parts into an intensifier meaning "extremely, thoroughly."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shífēn gǎnxiè nǐ.
examples.english: I'm extremely grateful to you.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge cài shífēn hǎochī.
examples.english: This dish is very delicious.

components.note: 酋 (wine jar) with a hand 寸 offering it: honoring a guest. 尊 sounds out 遵 zūn (obey) and 樽 zūn (goblet).
重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).

example.hanzi: 我们应该尊重每一个人的意见。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi zūnzhòng měi yí gè rén de yìjiàn.
example.english: We should respect everyone's opinions.
example.fact: 尊 alone pictures a wine jar 酋 lifted up by a hand 寸 — a gesture of offering made to an honored guest or ancestor — while 重 contributes the idea of "weight, importance"; together 尊重 treats respect almost literally as "holding someone up as important."

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zūnzhòng lǎorén.
examples.english: We should respect the elderly.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zūnzhòng wǒ de juédìng.
examples.english: Please respect my decision.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 授 is to hand over, to give.
受 (shòu) sounds exactly like 授.

example.hanzi: 张教授在国际会议上发表了演讲。
example.pinyin: Zhāng jiàoshòu zài guójì huìyì shàng fābiǎo le yǎnjiǎng.
example.english: Professor Zhang gave a speech at the international conference.
example.fact: 教授 is a genuine tone-based homograph: read jiàoshòu (as corrected here, 4th-tone 教) it's the everyday noun "professor" — overwhelmingly the common sense at this frequency, from news mentions of faculty to forms of address like 张教授 — while read jiāoshòu (1st-tone 教) it becomes a formal verb meaning "to instruct in a subject." The same split separates the everyday teaching verb 教 (jiāo, as in 教书) from the noun-forming reading 教 (jiào, as in 教育 "education").

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiàoshòu hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: My professor is very famous.

examples.pinyin: Wáng jiàoshòu, nín hǎo!
examples.english: Hello, Professor Wang!

components.note: 土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 去年夏天,我们去了云南旅行。
example.pinyin: Qùnián xiàtiān, wǒmen qù le Yúnnán lǜxíng.
example.english: Last summer, we traveled to Yunnan.
example.fact: 去年 uses 去 in its older sense of "past, gone by" rather than its everyday meaning "to go" — the same "past" sense survives in 去世 ("to pass away," lit. "to depart the world") — so 去年 literally reads as "the year gone by," a mirror image of 明年 ("next year") and 今年 ("this year").

examples.pinyin: Qùnián wǒ èrshí suì.
examples.english: Last year I was twenty.

examples.pinyin: Tā qùnián bāndàole Běijīng.
examples.english: He moved to Beijing last year.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 语 is language and spoken words.
吾 (wú) — loose hint — 语 is yǔ; 吾 also sounds out 悟 wù.

example.hanzi: 你会说几种语言？
example.pinyin: Nǐ huì shuō jǐ zhǒng yǔyán?
example.english: How many languages can you speak?
example.fact: 语 forms the names of languages: 汉语, 英语, 日语. It also appears in 语言 (language), 语法 (grammar), 成语 (idiom) and 自言自语 (to talk to oneself). In messaging, 语音 means a voice message.

examples.pinyin: Tā huì shuō sān zhǒng yǔyán.
examples.english: He can speak three languages.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jù huà de yǔqì bú tài hǎo.
examples.english: The tone of this sentence isn't very good.

components.note: 走 (run, walk) — movement: 起 rise, 越 cross, 赶 hurry, 趣; 超 is to jump over, surpass.
召 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 招 zhāo, 绍 shào, 照 zhào.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 参加比赛的人数超过了两百人。
example.pinyin: Cānjiā bǐsài de rénshù chāoguò le liǎng bǎi rén.
example.english: The number of people participating in the competition exceeded two hundred.
example.fact: 超过 combines 超 ("to overtake while running," built from 走 "to walk/run") with 过 ("to pass by, cross over") — both halves independently picture motion going beyond a point, reinforcing each other into a word that always implies comparison against some threshold or rival.

examples.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì chāoguòle wǒ.
examples.english: His grades surpassed mine.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé chāoguò yì bǎi mǐ kuān.
examples.english: This river is over a hundred meters wide.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (silk); 丝 is the simplified form of 絲, two skeins of silk side by side.

example.hanzi: 这件衣服是丝做的。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì sī zuò de.
example.english: This garment is made of silk.
example.fact: 丝 is silk thread and anything thread-like: 铁丝 (wire), 土豆丝 (shredded potato, a classic dish), 一丝笑容 (a trace of a smile). 丝绸之路 is the Silk Road, and 粉丝 means "fans", a pun on the English word with the noodle word.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo sījīn hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: This silk scarf is very pretty.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ niúròu qiē chéng xìsī.
examples.english: Please cut the beef into thin strips.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 他每天开车去上班。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān kāichē qù shàngbān.
example.english: He drives to work every day.
example.fact: 开车 literally means "to open/operate a car" — the same verb 开 that "opens" a door or a book also "operates" machines and vehicles in Chinese (开灯 "turn on the light," 开会 "hold a meeting"), a much broader use of "open" than English's narrower literal sense.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì kāichē ma?
examples.english: Can you drive?

examples.pinyin: Kāichē de shíhou bié kàn shǒujī.
examples.english: Don't look at your phone while driving.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; here the word for still or again.
乃 (nǎi) is a loose sound hint; 扔 rēng shares the same part.

example.hanzi: 他仍然住在老房子里。
example.pinyin: Tā réngrán zhù zài lǎo fángzi lǐ.
example.english: He still lives in the old house.
example.fact: 仍 is a formal adverb for "still": 仍然, 仍旧. In everyday speech people more naturally say 还 or 还是. You will meet 仍 more in writing, news and reports than in casual talk.

examples.hanzi: 雨下了一天，现在仍在下。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ xià le yì tiān, xiànzài réng zài xià.
examples.english: It has rained all day and it's still raining now.

examples.hanzi: 虽然很累，他仍旧坚持工作。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán hěn lèi, tā réngjiù jiānchí gōngzuò.
examples.english: Although he's tired, he still keeps working.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — marks houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 室 room, 客 guest; 寄 is sending something to live at a place, then to mail.
奇 (qí) — loose sound hint (jì vs qí); 奇 also sounds out 骑 qí and 椅 yǐ.

example.hanzi: 我想寄一封信。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jì yì fēng xìn.
example.english: I want to mail a letter.
example.fact: 寄 is to send by post or courier: 寄信, 寄快递, 邮寄. It also means to lodge or entrust: 寄宿 (board at school), 寄托 (to pin hopes on). 寄 is for mailing, whereas 送 is to deliver or give by hand.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我把这个包裹寄到上海。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ zhège bāoguǒ jì dào Shànghǎi.
examples.english: Please help me mail this parcel to Shanghai.

examples.hanzi: 我把行李寄放在朋友家。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ xíngli jìfàng zài péngyou jiā.
examples.english: I left my luggage at a friend's place.

components.note: Four mouths 口 (vessels) with a dog 犬 guarding them — the traditional explanation; 器 is any vessel or tool, as in 武器 and 机器.

example.hanzi: 这个机器是新的。
example.pinyin: Zhège jīqì shì xīn de.
example.english: This machine is new.
example.fact: 器 is a bound word for devices and containers: 机器 (machine), 武器 (weapon), 乐器 (musical instrument), 电器 (appliance), 器官 (organ). The idiom 大器晚成 means a great talent matures late.

examples.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ yǒu hěn duō qìjù.
examples.english: There are many utensils in the kitchen.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhǒng xīnxíng de diànqì.
examples.english: This is a new type of electrical appliance.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 聊 is a chat, with ears open.
卯 (mǎo) is a loose sound clue; same part in 柳 liǔ, 留 liú, 贸 mào.

example.hanzi: 我们坐下来聊聊吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò xiàlái liáoliao ba.
example.english: Let's sit down and chat.
example.fact: 聊 is casual chatting, usually reduplicated or as 聊天 (to chat, including text chat). 无聊 means bored or boring: the older sense of 聊 was "to depend on", so it is something with nothing to hold on to.

examples.hanzi: 下班后我们去咖啡馆聊天。
examples.pinyin: Xiàbān hòu wǒmen qù kāfēiguǎn liáotiān.
examples.english: After work we go chat at a café.

examples.hanzi: 我们没聊几句，他就走了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen méi liáo jǐ jù, tā jiù zǒu le.
examples.english: We barely chatted before he left.

meanings: the arches, loops and whorls on the fingers

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 纹 is the pattern of threads.
文 (wén) sounds exactly like 纹; also in 蚊 wén.

example.hanzi: 手机可以用指纹解锁。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī kěyǐ yòng zhǐwén jiěsuǒ.
example.english: You can unlock the phone using your fingerprint.
example.fact: 指纹 combines 指 ("finger") with 纹 ("pattern, grain" — the same root behind 花纹 "decorative pattern" and 纹路 "grain lines"), treating a fingerprint as just one more example of a natural surface pattern, the same way wood grain or a leaf's veins would be described.

examples.hanzi: 这扇门要用指纹才能打开。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shàn mén yào yòng zhǐwén cáinéng dǎkāi.
examples.english: This door can only be opened with a fingerprint.

examples.hanzi: 警察在杯子上发现了指纹。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài bēizi shàng fāxiànle zhǐwén.
examples.english: The police found fingerprints on the cup.

components.note: 广 (house) — the cover on top, as in 店 shop. It marks a room or hall where people celebrate.
大 (big) — the part inside the house. Dictionary story: a great (大) event in a house; 庆祝 celebrate. Memory aid, as 庆 is simplified from 慶.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and prayer: 神, 礼, 福, 祈; 祝 is to wish.
兄 (older brother) — an opened mouth before the altar: the one who speaks the prayer or blessing.

example.hanzi: 我们打算庆祝他的生日。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎsuàn qìngzhù tā de shēngrì.
example.english: We plan to celebrate his birthday.
example.fact: 庆祝 reinforces two overlapping ideas — 庆 ("to celebrate," pictured as a grand event 大 held under a roof 广) and 祝 ("to wish, pray for blessings," with the altar radical 礻) — pairing a worldly celebration with a spoken blessing, the same double-barreled word-building strategy seen in 喜欢 and 应该 in the character deck's own word list.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ qìngzhù xīnnián ba.
examples.english: Let's celebrate the new year together.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā jǔbēi qìngzhù shènglì.
examples.english: Everyone raised their glasses to celebrate the victory.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 住手!你会伤到他的。
example.pinyin: Zhùshǒu! Nǐ huì shāng dào tā de.
example.english: Stop! You'll hurt him.
example.fact: 住手 literally means "to halt the hand" (住 "to stop, stay" + 手 "hand") — used as a sharp command, it belongs to a small family of "stop + body part" imperatives that includes 住口 ("shut your mouth," lit. "stop the mouth"), each naming the specific body part responsible for the unwanted action.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhùshǒu, bié dǎ le.
examples.english: Please stop, don't fight.

examples.hanzi: 两个孩子听到老师的话就住手了。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge háizi tīngdào lǎoshī de huà jiù zhùshǒu le.
examples.english: The two kids stopped when they heard the teacher.

components.note: 女 (woman) — mothers and girls: 妈, 姑, 姐; 娘 is mother or young woman, as in 新娘 bride.
良 (liáng) is a loose sound hint (-iang); same part in 狼 láng and 浪 làng.

example.hanzi: 她回娘家看望父母。
example.pinyin: Tā huí niángjiā kànwàng fùmǔ.
example.english: She's going back to her parents' home to visit them.
example.fact: 娘 is a colloquial "mother" (爹娘 mom and dad). It appears in 娘家 (a married woman's parental home), 新娘 (bride) and 姑娘 (girl, young woman, read gūniang).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ niángjiā zài nánfāng.
examples.english: My mother's family home is in the south.

examples.pinyin: Tā duì zìjǐ de niáng hěn xiàoshùn.
examples.english: He is very devoted to his mother.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 偶 first meant a figure or doll, then a pair.
禺 (yú) is a loose sound clue; same part in 遇 yù, 愚 yú, 寓 yù.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 像 is a person's likeness.
象 (xiàng, elephant) gives the exact sound; 象 first meant elephant, then "image".

example.hanzi: 很多年轻人把这位歌手当作自己的偶像。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō niánqīng rén bǎ zhè wèi gēshǒu dàngzuò zìjǐ de ǒuxiàng.
example.english: Many young people regard this singer as their idol.
example.fact: 偶像 originally referred literally to a carved wooden or clay figure worshipped as a god — 偶 (from the person radical 亻) meant "a figure, statue" before it took on its other senses "by chance" and "a couple" — and the compound carried that image of a worshipped effigy forward into its modern, secular sense of a celebrity idolized by fans.

examples.hanzi: 我的偶像是一位篮球运动员。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de ǒuxiàng shì yí wèi lánqiú yùndòngyuán.
examples.english: My idol is a basketball player.

examples.hanzi: 她在家里贴满了偶像的海报。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiālǐ tiēmǎnle ǒuxiàng de hǎibào.
examples.english: She covered her home with posters of her idol.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
心 (heart) — feelings and will: 想, 思, 感; 志 is what the heart is set on, ambition.
士 (shì) is only a loose sound hint for zhì.

example.hanzi: 各位同志,请注意会议时间的变化。
example.pinyin: Gèwèi tóngzhì, qǐng zhùyì huìyì shíjiān de biànhuà.
example.english: Comrades, please note the change in meeting time.
example.fact: 同志 literally means "same aspiration" (同 "same" + 志 "ambition, will") and was the standard, egalitarian form of address in Mao-era China, much as "comrade" was used in other socialist movements; since around the late 1980s it has also become common slang for "homosexual" in Chinese-speaking communities, an entirely separate modern reappropriation of the same old political word.

examples.hanzi: 老同志们都来参加了会议。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo tóngzhìmen dōu lái cānjiāle huìyì.
examples.english: The veteran comrades all came to attend the meeting.

examples.pinyin: Tóngzhìmen, dàjiā xīnkǔ le!
examples.english: Comrades, thank you all for your hard work!

components.note: 衤 (clothing, 衣字旁) — clothes: 衬 shirt, 衫, 裙 skirt, 被 quilt; 裤 is trousers.
库 (kù) sounds exactly like 裤.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 这条裤子有点儿长,得改一改。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi yǒudiǎnr cháng, děi gǎi yi gǎi.
example.english: These pants are a bit long; they need to be altered.
example.fact: 裤子 takes the clothing radical 衤 (a compressed form of 衣, "clothing," also seen in 衬衫 "shirt" and 裙子 "skirt") paired with the phonetic 库 (kù, "storehouse") purely for its sound — a reminder that the radical, not the phonetic half, is usually the more reliable guide to a character's meaning.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi duōshao qián?
examples.english: How much are these trousers?

examples.hanzi: 他穿了一条黑色的裤子。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuānle yì tiáo hēisè de kùzi.
examples.english: He wore a pair of black trousers.

components.note: 车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.

example.hanzi: 这个国家的军队负责保卫边境。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de jūnduì fùzé bǎowèi biānjìng.
example.english: This country's military is responsible for defending the border.
example.fact: 军队 combines 军 (an old pictograph of soldiers riding out in war chariots 车) with 队 ("a team, a file of people," from an image of people 人 gathered together) — forming the general word for any organized armed force, from a national army down to a smaller unit.

examples.hanzi: 他在军队里服役了两年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jūnduì lǐ fúyìle liǎng nián.
examples.english: He served in the army for two years.

examples.hanzi: 军队帮助人们处理了洪水。
examples.pinyin: Jūnduì bāngzhù rénmen chǔlǐle hóngshuǐ.
examples.english: The army helped people deal with the flood.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 假 is to borrow or fake, a person lending a false front.
叚 (jiǎ) sounds like 假; also in 暇 xiá and 霞 xiá.
衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 他假装没听到我说的话。
example.pinyin: Tā jiǎzhuāng méi tīngdào wǒ shuō de huà.
example.english: He pretended not to hear what I said.
example.fact: 假 on its own already means “fake, false” (as in 假货, “counterfeit goods”), and 装 can independently mean “to dress up, put on an act” (装傻, “play dumb”) — 假装 stacks two words that both point toward artifice, a common way Mandarin builds a two-character verb from near-synonyms.

examples.hanzi: 别假装生病了，我知道你没事。
examples.pinyin: Bié jiǎzhuāng shēngbìng le, wǒ zhīdào nǐ méi shì.
examples.english: Stop pretending to be sick, I know you're fine.

examples.hanzi: 他假装睡着了，其实一直在听。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎzhuāng shuìzháo le, qíshí yìzhí zài tīng.
examples.english: He pretended to be asleep, but he was listening all along.

components.note: 心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.

example.hanzi: 这首歌让我想起了童年。
example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē ràng wǒ xiǎngqǐ le tóngnián.
example.english: This song reminds me of my childhood.
example.fact: 想起 is a verb-plus-complement pair: 想 (“to think”) combines with 起, literally “to rise,” used here as a directional complement — a memory “rising up” into awareness. The same 起 carries a related sense in 起来's “coming into being” usage.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qǐlái le, tā jiào Xiǎo Wáng.
examples.english: I remember now, his name is Xiao Wang.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎngqǐ shénme le ma?
examples.english: Did you think of something?

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 侦 is a person who scouts.
贞 (zhēn) sounds exactly like 侦.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 探 is to reach out and feel, then to explore.
The right half is a sound part shared with 深 shēn: a loose clue for tàn.

example.hanzi: 那位侦探很快就找到了线索。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi zhēntàn hěn kuài jiù zhǎodào le xiànsuǒ.
example.english: That detective quickly found a clue.
example.fact: 侦探 as a compound job title pairs two overlapping “to investigate” verbs — 侦 (“to scout, spy on”) and 探 (“to probe, explore”) — reinforcing near-synonyms into one word, a common Mandarin word-building strategy.

examples.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo jiù xiǎng dāng zhēntàn.
examples.english: He has wanted to be a detective since he was little.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn zhēntàn xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: I like reading detective novels.

components.note: 犭 (dog, animal) — animals, as in 狗, 猫, 猪: a wild animal.
王 (wáng) is a loose sound clue for kuáng; 王 also in 往 wǎng and 旺 wàng.

example.hanzi: 他们在街上狂欢。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài jiē shang kuánghuān.
example.english: They are partying wildly in the street.
example.fact: 狂 means wild or mad and also arrogant: 疯狂 (crazy), 狂欢 (revel; 狂欢节 is a carnival), 狂妄 (arrogant), 狂风 (gale).

examples.pinyin: Tāmen gāoxìng de fākuáng.
examples.english: They were wild with joy.

examples.hanzi: 他口气很狂，谁也不放在眼里。
examples.pinyin: Tā kǒuqì hěn kuáng, shéi yě bú fàng zài yǎn lǐ.
examples.english: He is very arrogant and looks down on everyone.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — hand actions; 拖 is to drag, as in 拉 pull, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 他把桌子拖到了门口。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhuōzi tuō dào le ménkǒu.
example.english: He dragged the table to the door.
example.fact: 拖 is to drag or tow: 拖地 (mop the floor), 拖鞋 (slippers, "dragged shoes"), 拖拉机 (tractor, "dragging machine"). It also means to put things off: 拖延 (procrastinate).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié tuō wǒ de hòutuǐ.
examples.english: Don't hold me back.

examples.hanzi: 他把作业拖到最后一天才写。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zuòyè tuō dào zuìhòu yì tiān cái xiě.
examples.english: He put off his homework until the last day.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
马 (horse) — horses: 骑, 驾, 骄; 验 first meant testing a horse, then any test.
佥 (qiān) gives the -ian rhyme; same part in 险 xiǎn, 检 jiǎn, 脸 liǎn, 签 qiān.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 科学家们在实验室里做实验。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā men zài shíyànshì lǐ zuò shíyàn.
example.english: The scientists are doing experiments in the laboratory.
example.fact: 实验室 is just 实验 (“experiment,” from 实 “real, actual” + 验 “to test, verify”) plus the suffix 室 (“room”) — the same room-naming suffix behind 教室 (“classroom”) and 办公室 (“office”), a reliable pattern for naming a room by what happens inside it.

examples.hanzi: 学生们在实验室里很认真。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen zài shíyànshì lǐ hěn rènzhēn.
examples.english: The students are very serious in the laboratory.

examples.pinyin: Shíyànshì lǐ bù néng chī dōngxi.
examples.english: You can't eat in the laboratory.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — heads and faces: 头, 额 forehead, 题 title, 领 collar; 顺 is a head following the river 川 along.
川 (chuān) is only a loose sound hint; 训 xùn and 顺 shùn share it.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do. 便 is a person adjusting things 更 to make them convenient (traditional explanation).

example.hanzi: 你去超市的话,顺便帮我买一瓶牛奶吧。
example.pinyin: Nǐ qù chāoshì dehuà, shùnbiàn bāng wǒ mǎi yì píng niúnǎi ba.
example.english: If you're going to the supermarket, could you pick up a bottle of milk for me while you're at it?
example.fact: 顺便 almost always attaches to a request or suggestion (顺便 + verb), politely framing a favor as no extra trouble — it signals the action is being done “along the way,” piggybacking on something already planned, much like English “while you're at it.”

examples.hanzi: 我出门的时候，顺便把垃圾扔了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chūmén de shíhou, shùnbiàn bǎ lājī rēng le.
examples.english: I threw out the trash on my way out.

examples.hanzi: 顺便问一下，你明天有空吗？
examples.pinyin: Shùnbiàn wèn yíxià, nǐ míngtiān yǒu kòng ma?
examples.english: By the way, are you free tomorrow?

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 吹 is blowing, and 欠 on the right shows a person with open mouth exhaling.
欠 (yawn) — an open mouth breathing out; same part in 歌 song and 次 time.

example.hanzi: 风把门吹开了。
example.pinyin: Fēng bǎ mén chuī kāi le.
example.english: The wind blew the door open.
example.fact: 吹 is to blow: 吹风机 (hair dryer), 吹气球 (blow up a balloon) and 吹笛子 (play a flute). 吹牛 ("blow a cow") means to brag, and in slang 吹了 can mean a relationship or deal fell through.

examples.pinyin: Tā huì chuī dízi.
examples.english: He can play the flute.

examples.pinyin: Bié chuīniú le, wǒ bú xìn.
examples.english: Stop bragging; I don't believe it.

components.note: 害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.

example.hanzi: 吸烟有害健康。
example.pinyin: Xīyān yǒu hài jiànkāng.
example.english: Smoking is harmful to health.
example.fact: 害 is to harm: 伤害 (injure), 害虫 (pest), 有害 (harmful). It also has feeling words: 害怕 (afraid), 害羞 (shy). In online slang a drawn-out 害 conveys a sigh of resignation.

examples.pinyin: Bié hàipà, wǒ zài zhèlǐ.
examples.english: Don't be afraid; I'm here.

examples.pinyin: Áoyè duì shēntǐ yǒu hài.
examples.english: Staying up late is harmful to your health.

components.note: 戈 (halberd) — a weapon guarding a place 口: 或 first meant a defended territory (域 yù adds 土). "Perhaps, or" is a later use.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 你可以喝茶或是喝咖啡。
example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ hē chá huòshì hē kāfēi.
example.english: You can drink tea or coffee.
example.fact: 或 alone can already mean “or” by itself; the following 是 isn't the verb “to be” here but a light, semantically bleached suffix that pads a one-syllable connector into a smoother two-syllable one — a similar non-literal role 是 plays in conjunctions like 但是 (“but”) and 要是 (“if”).

examples.hanzi: 周末我们去看电影或是去逛街。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù kàn diànyǐng huòshì qù guàngjiē.
examples.english: At the weekend we'll go to a movie or go shopping.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng chī mǐfàn huòshì miàntiáo?
examples.english: Would you like rice or noodles?

components.note: 彡 (decorative strokes) — marks patterns and adornment, as in 形 shape, 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 修 is to tidy and decorate, then repair.
攸 (yōu) is only a loose hint for xiū; 悠 yōu shares it.

example.hanzi: 我的电脑坏了，要找人修。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de diànnǎo huài le, yào zhǎo rén xiū.
example.english: My computer is broken and needs someone to fix it.
example.fact: 修 is to repair or improve: 修理 (repair), 修改 (revise), 修路 (repair roads), 装修 (renovate a home). It also means study or self-cultivation: 进修 (further study), 修养 (accomplishment), 修炼 (cultivate oneself).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ xiū yíxià zìxíngchē.
examples.english: Please help me fix my bike.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù zhèngzài xiū, bùnéng zǒu.
examples.english: This road is under repair and can't be used.

meanings: (often used in the negative) to care about

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.
乎 (hū) — as a sound part it gives hū to 呼 (call out, breathe out), so 呼 and 乎 sound the same.

example.hanzi: 别人怎么想,他一点也不在乎。
example.pinyin: Biérén zěnme xiǎng, tā yìdiǎn yě bú zàihu.
example.english: He doesn't care at all what other people think.
example.fact: Although older dictionary senses for 在乎 include formal phrases like “to rest with” or “to be due to,” in everyday Mandarin it overwhelmingly means “to care” — and it shows up far more often in its negative form 不在乎 (“doesn't care”) than as a bare positive claim, much as English “mind” reads more naturally in “I don't mind” than in a positive statement.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú zàihu zhè diǎn xiǎoshì.
examples.english: I don't mind this little thing.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn zàihu péngyou de kànfǎ.
examples.english: She cares a lot about her friends' opinions.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 聊 is a chat, with ears open.
卯 (mǎo) is a loose sound clue; same part in 柳 liǔ, 留 liú, 贸 mào.

example.hanzi: 这部电影太无聊了,我们中途就走了。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng tài wúliáo le, wǒmen zhōngtú jiù zǒu le.
example.english: This movie was so boring that we left partway through.
example.fact: 无聊 can describe either the boring situation or the bored person feeling it, without changing form — Mandarin adjectives like this rely entirely on context to sort out the active/passive reading that English marks with “-ing” versus “-ed” (boring vs. bored).

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān zhēn wúliáo, méiyǒu shì zuò.
examples.english: Today is so boring with nothing to do.

examples.hanzi: 我觉得他讲的笑话很无聊。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde tā jiǎng de xiàohua hěn wúliáo.
examples.english: I think the jokes he tells are lame.

components.note: 犬 (dog) — animals: 狗, 猫; 状 first meant the shape of an animal.
丬 (a form of 爿) gives zhuàng: also in 壮 zhuàng, 装 zhuāng, 将 jiāng and 奖 jiǎng.
兄 (xiōng) is only a loose sound clue for kuàng; the radical here is the ice form of 氵, as in 決.

example.hanzi: 医生说她的身体状况已经稳定了。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā de shēntǐ zhuàngkuàng yǐjīng wěndìng le.
example.english: The doctor said her physical condition has stabilized.
example.fact: 状况 and its near-synonym 情况 both translate as “situation,” but 状况 leans toward a measurable, observable state — health, equipment, finances — while 情况 more often frames a broader, unfolding circumstance, a distinction dictionaries frequently gloss identically.

examples.hanzi: 公司现在的经济状况不太好。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī xiànzài de jīngjì zhuàngkuàng bú tài hǎo.
examples.english: The company's financial condition isn't very good now.

examples.hanzi: 路上的交通状况怎么样？
examples.pinyin: Lùshang de jiāotōng zhuàngkuàng zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: What are the traffic conditions on the road?

components.note: 目 (eye) — an eye turned on its side. As a radical it marks sight: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睡 sleep, 盯 stare.
白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 他学中文的目的是想去中国工作。
example.pinyin: Tā xué Zhōngwén de mùdì shì xiǎng qù Zhōngguó gōngzuò.
example.english: His purpose in learning Chinese is to go work in China.
example.fact: 目的 combines 目 (“eye”) with 的, which in Classical Chinese specifically meant “a target for archery” — literally “what the eye is aimed at,” a vivid compositional image behind today's abstract word for “purpose, goal.”

examples.hanzi: 这次开会的目的是什么？
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kāihuì de mùdì shì shénme?
examples.english: What is the purpose of this meeting?

examples.hanzi: 他来这里的目的不明确。
examples.pinyin: Tā lái zhèlǐ de mùdì bù míngquè.
examples.english: The purpose of his coming here is unclear.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.
鬼 (ghost) — spirits and the unseen: 魂, 魅, 愧; 魔 is a demon.
麻 (má) is a near sound match for mó; also in 磨 mó and 摩 mó.

example.hanzi: 故事里的恶魔想要毁灭整个世界。
example.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de èmó xiǎng yào huǐmiè zhěng gè shìjiè.
example.english: The demon in the story wants to destroy the entire world.
example.fact: 魔 was coined specifically to carry a foreign sound: early Buddhist translators first wrote Sanskrit “māra” (a demon who tempted the Buddha) as 磨 (“to grind”), and Emperor Wu of Liang is credited with swapping its 石 radical for 鬼 (“ghost”) to produce 魔 — one of a small set of Chinese characters invented mainly to carry a loanword's sound, later broadening into today's everyday word for “demon, magic.”

examples.hanzi: 孩子们害怕童话里的恶魔。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen hàipà tónghuà lǐ de èmó.
examples.english: The kids are afraid of the demon in the fairy tale.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏里有很多恶魔。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge yóuxì lǐ yǒu hěn duō èmó.
examples.english: There are many demons in this game.

components.note: 石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.

example.hanzi: 请检查门窗,确保一切安全。
example.pinyin: Qǐng jiǎnchá ménchuāng, quèbǎo yíqiè ānquán.
example.english: Please check the doors and windows to make sure everything is safe.
example.fact: 确保 sits at the formal end of Mandarin's “make sure” vocabulary — official announcements, safety instructions, and contracts reach for it, where casual speech more often just uses 保证 (“promise, guarantee”) or a plain 一定 (“definitely”); using 确保 in everyday conversation can sound a little stiff.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào quèbǎo zìjǐ de ānquán.
examples.english: You need to make sure you're safe.

examples.hanzi: 老师确保每个学生都听懂了。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī quèbǎo měi ge xuésheng dōu tīngdǒng le.
examples.english: The teacher made sure every student understood.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; 脏 is an organ (zàng), and also dirty (zāng).
庄 (zhuāng) is a near sound match for zàng/zāng; also in 装 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 医生用听诊器检查了他的心脏。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng yòng tīngzhěnqì jiǎnchá le tā de xīnzàng.
example.english: The doctor used a stethoscope to examine his heart.
example.fact: 心脏 is the precise anatomical term for the physical heart organ, built from 心 (“heart”) plus 脏 (zàng, “internal organ”) — for the emotional or figurative “heart” (feelings, courage, the heart of a matter), Mandarin instead reaches for the bare 心 alone, a split English's single word “heart” doesn't make.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xīnzàng tiào de hěn kuài.
examples.english: My heart is beating very fast.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷的心脏不太好，要多注意。
examples.pinyin: Yéye de xīnzàng bú tài hǎo, yào duō zhùyì.
examples.english: Grandpa's heart isn't very good, so be careful.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 像 resemble; 似 is to look like.
以 (yǐ) is only a loose sound hint for sì.
白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 他跑得飞快,像箭似的。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎo de fēikuài, xiàng jiàn shìde.
example.english: He ran incredibly fast, like an arrow.
example.fact: 似 is pronounced sì almost everywhere else in Mandarin (相似, “similar”), but Mainland dictionaries specifically mark this one grammatical suffix as shìde — Taiwan usage instead keeps the more predictable sìde, making 似的 one of the few words where the Mainland-standard reading is the less intuitive one to memorize.

examples.pinyin: Tā gāoxìng de xiàng háizi shìde.
examples.english: She was as happy as a child.

examples.hanzi: 他看起来像没睡醒似的。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlái xiàng méi shuìxǐng shìde.
examples.english: He looks like he hasn't woken up.

components.note: 舛 (two opposed feet) — the dancer's footwork; 無 (wú) above is a loose sound clue, as it once meant dance itself.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 学校下周六举办一场舞会。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào xià zhōu liù jǔbàn yì chǎng wǔhuì.
example.english: The school is holding a dance next Saturday.
example.fact: 舞会 pairs 舞 (“dance”) with 会 in its “gathering, meeting” sense — the same sense behind 社会 (“society,” also in this batch) — rather than 会's more familiar “to know how to” sense, a reminder that the character carries two genuinely separate meanings depending on context.

examples.pinyin: Míngwǎn de wǔhuì nǐ qù ma?
examples.english: Are you going to tomorrow night's dance?

examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǔhuì shàng yùdàole tā.
examples.english: She met him at the dance.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 急 is a heart in a hurry. The top is a variant of 及 (jí, reach), the same sound as in 级 and 极.

example.hanzi: 别急，慢慢来。
example.pinyin: Bié jí, mànmàn lái.
example.english: Don't worry, take your time.
example.fact: 急 is anxious or urgent: 着急 (to worry, be impatient), 急事 (urgent matter), 急诊 (emergency room). Say 他急了 to mean "he got flustered or lost patience".

examples.pinyin: Tā jí zhe qù jīchǎng.
examples.english: He is in a hurry to get to the airport.

examples.hanzi: 这件事很急，请马上处理。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì hěn jí, qǐng mǎshàng chǔlǐ.
examples.english: This is urgent; please deal with it right away.

components.note: 風 (traditional wind) — 风 is the simplified form of 風, which had 凡 (fán) as a loose sound hint around 虫; the simplified shape is just a reduced form.

example.hanzi: 今天的风很大。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de fēng hěn dà.
example.english: The wind is strong today.
example.fact: 风 is wind and, extended, custom or style: 风俗 (customs), 风景 (scenery), 作风 (style of conduct). 风水 ("wind and water") is the practice of feng shui, and 台风 is a typhoon.

examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān de fēng hěn lěng.
examples.english: The winter wind is very cold.

examples.pinyin: Fēng chuī de shùyè shāshā xiǎng.
examples.english: The wind makes the leaves rustle.

components.note: 而 (and; an old picture of a beard) — the top part. The dictionary story is a woman in a false beard having fun (play-acting); a memory aid.
女 (woman) — the bottom. Used in 耍赖 act shamelessly, 玩耍 to play, 耍帅 to show off.

example.hanzi: 别耍小聪明。
example.pinyin: Bié shuǎ xiǎo cōngming.
example.english: Don't try to be clever.
example.fact: 耍 is to play or fool around, and to play a trick: 耍赖 (act shamelessly), 耍帅 (show off), 耍心眼 (scheme). In Sichuan dialect 耍 is the everyday word for "hang out" or "play".

examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì shuǎlài, bù jiǎng dàolǐ.
examples.english: He always acts shamelessly and won't listen to reason.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在公园里耍得很开心。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài gōngyuán lǐ shuǎ de hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: The kids are having great fun playing in the park.
